medmemorybench.question: Which language did the paper baselines use?
medmemorybench.answer: The paper never states it. Evidence points to Chinese (inferred, not stated).
evidence: Paper text (pdftotext of arxiv.org/pdf/2605.11814): the words Chinese, English, bilingual and language do not occur outside the reference list; Section 6.1 only says "All baselines employ GPT-5.1 as the backbone model, with Claude-4-Sonnet serving as the judge model."
Table 2 reports a second (Mixed, noise) column for every method; Section 4.2 builds the noise from "General health knowledge consultations" and "Proxy consultations for family members".

HF card (Cyan27/MedMemoryBench README, data layout note): "noise_sessions.parquet is only available for the Chinese (zh) split as the standalone noise session data was generated exclusively in Chinese."
GitHub repo configs/dataset_config/medmemorybench.yaml: language "zh", root_dir data/MedMemoryBench (Chinese); the English data is a second root_dir (README: data/MedMemoryBench_EN).
medmemorybench.consequence: Run the zh split to compare with Table 2 (the 1,939 queries are the same in both). Ask the authors if the exact language matters.

discrepancies: ResearchClawBench: data + related_work of the ten tasks is 606 MB, just over the 600 MB bar; the 78 MB paper_001.pdf of Information_004 was made large-only so 527 MB was fetched.
EvoClawBench has no medical-document group (see the entry note); the plan should say Healthcare family (5 tasks, 25 sub-problems, 25 cases) instead.
CIMemories: 49 contexts per profile in the file against 45 in the paper; GitHub reports the license as other but the LICENSE file is CC BY-NC 4.0.
PrecisionMemBench: the HF dataset is only a leaderboard; the 89 cases live in the GitHub repository.
WebShop: the 1.18 M-product data is not in the repository (Google Drive, not pinned).
